title: tool.call
description: An agent invoked a tool. This is what makes the thread timeline evidence rather than conversation: a durable, signed record that an action was attempted, by which agent, with which tool, against what target. It deliberately carries no tool arguments. Arguments are model-generated free-form text, they are the place where secrets and reasoning reach the wire, and this event is replicated and retained for the life of the stream; the verbatim arguments stay in the local raw capture and are bound to this record by arguments_digest.

call_id.description: Correlates this call with the tool.result that answers it. Minted by the publisher - the Conductor process that observes the invocation - as a UUIDv7, and never taken from the harness: harness call identifiers differ in shape between harnesses, are unique only within one session, and are not values this protocol controls. Because it is a protocol identifier it is also safe on a subject.

agent_id.description: The agent that made the call. Attribution is required, not derived from the envelope: an event that has been forwarded is still readable on its own, and 'who did this' is the first question asked of any tool record.

activity_id.description: The activity the call belongs to, when the agent is executing one. It scopes the call to a unit of work that has a plan, a lease, and a budget.

tool_name.description: The tool the agent invoked, as its harness names it - for example "bash", "read_file", or an MCP tool name. A name only; never a rendered invocation.

target.description: What the call acted on, structured so that a timeline can be filtered, gated, and audited without anyone parsing an argument blob. Omitted when the publisher cannot derive a single target: an emitter that would have to concatenate arguments to fill this in must publish no target instead.

kind.description: path: a filesystem path, file or directory. command: the executable or subcommand invoked, without its arguments. url: a network endpoint. resource: anything else addressable by a stable name, such as an MCP resource or a record identifier.

reference.description: The target itself, bounded and passed through the redaction pass before publication. It is one reference, not a command line and not an argument dump; when redaction fired, redacted is true.

arguments_digest.description: sha256 over the RFC 8785 canonical form of the arguments the tool was called with. It binds this record to one specific invocation, so a later dispute can be settled against the local raw capture without the arguments ever being published.
